title: lab.common.store.Store wired into brain.reason as a RAG connector, via the existing duck-typed connector= extension point
goal: Give lab.common.store.Store -- a confirmed-dormant, zero-real-caller module -- its first real regression test as brain.reason's actual RAG backend, closing the gap the project owner's own architecture description named: data fetched from an external source should be vectorized and retrievable by the brain, not re-supplied as direct passages on every call.
method: Four small, mixed-topic passages built into a Store (lexical + dense bge leg, RRF-fused) and persisted to disk; a second, brand-new Store instance loads that same collection back (real persistence, not reuse of the in-process object) and is passed as reason()'s connector= argument with passages=[] -- forcing every answer to come from the connector, not from direct passages. Two on-topic asks (each needing a different one of two Ravi-related passages to be the one that actually surfaces), one off-topic ask (checking the connector's irrelevant top-k doesn't get treated as grounding), and one same-ask-no-connector baseline (isolating the Store's real effect).

case2_ravi_address.text: Ravi Sharma lives at 14 MG Road, Pune 411001. [S0]

baseline_same_ask_no_connector.text: [Not grounded in any provided evidence -- general knowledge only.] The notice period is the time it takes for a notice to be issued.

results_prose: With a Store connector (dense+lexical, RRF-fused, reloaded fresh from disk): 'What is the notice period?' -> decision='supported', text='30 days [S3]' (fetched ['S3', 'S1']). 'Where does Ravi Sharma live?' -> decision='supported', text='Ravi Sharma lives at 14 MG Road, Pune 411001. [S0]' (fetched ['S0', 'S1']). Off-topic 'What is the capital of France?' -> decision='inconclusive' (fetched ['S3', 'S0'], none relevant, correctly not used as grounding). Same notice-period ask with no connector at all -> decision='ungrounded' -- confirms the Store, not some pre-existing capability, is what answered case1.
conclusion: lab.common.store.Store works as a lab.common.brain.reason RAG backend end to end, through the existing connector= extension point, with zero new production code: build once, reload from disk in a new Store instance, hand it to reason() as connector=, and the right passage is retrieved and cited correctly for two different asks, while an off-topic ask that retrieves only irrelevant passages is correctly NOT answered as supported -- the connector supplies candidates, reason()'s own grounding logic still decides what counts as evidence. The same ask with no connector at all does not answer, isolating the Store's real contribution rather than crediting it for something reason() could already do. This closes the one concrete, confirmed gap in the project owner's own architecture description: 'our system fetch data from these places... this data should also be vectorised rag'.
scale_down: Four passages, one collection, two real asks plus one off-topic and one baseline -- a proof the wiring works end to end, not a retrieval-quality benchmark at corpus scale (lab.common.store's own module docstring already covers the RRF-fusion design rationale separately).
follow_ups: Not yet exercised with Store's use_graph=True leg (entity-graph expansion) or Store.upsert's incremental-ingest path through reason() -- this exploration only proves the base build+load+search path.

connector_top_k=2 was chosen to keep the fixture's retrieval precision meaningful (so the right passage has to actually outrank the other Ravi passage, not just be included among four); untested at the larger top_k a real multi-hundred-passage collection would use.

No caller in this repo builds a Store from real documents yet (lab.common.ingest.chunk_document + Store.build/ingest_and_store exist and are callable, but nothing in lab/ does this outside this exploration's own fixture) -- the next real step is a caller that ingests an actual document into a Store collection before any ask arrives, rather than building fixture passages inline.
models_used: bge-small-en-v1.5 (lab.common.real_encoders, Store's dense leg) -- non-generative similarity scoring only; brain.reason's own classical lookup path answers from the retrieved passages, same as every other direct-passages caller.
